entrypoints.summary: A caller invokes TokenMigrator.migrate(uint256 amount), supplying an amount denominated in source-token base units; the finding concerns deployments whose configured source and target tokens have different decimal precision.

affected_components.role: The reported migration path withdraws target tokens using the unchanged caller amount.

code_slices.fixed: The report specifies constructor/deployment validation requiring sourceToken.decimals() == targetToken.decimals().
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report states that this path assumes both tokens have identical decimal places.
code_slices.vulnerable: migrate() calls _withdraw(i_targetToken, _msgSender(), amount) using amount without decimal scaling.

negative_controls: Use tokens with matching decimal places.
Reject deployment when sourceToken.decimals() differs from targetToken.decimals().
observability.positive_marker: In the report's 18-to-6 example, a one-token source migration pays 1×10^18 target base units, or 1×10^12 target tokens.

preconditions: A migration deployment uses source and target ERC-20 tokens with unequal decimal places.
The caller can submit a migration transaction and the lockbox has sufficient target-token inventory for the resulting transfer.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: For the stated 18-decimal-to-6-decimal case, amount = 1×10^18 for one source token.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit migrate(amount) with amount expressed in source-token base units; the contract deposits the source amount and withdraws the identical integer amount of target-token base units.

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that differing token decimal places combined with unchanged integer transfer make the migration value-discrepant.
The report's 18-to-6 and 6-to-18 examples show that the same integer represents a drastically different target-token economic quantity.
For the 18-decimal to 6-decimal configuration described in the report, an unchanged amount yields 1×10^12 target tokens for a one-token source migration.
The report identifies significant financial losses among the consequences of decimal-mismatched migrations.
The report recommends and describes resolution through a deployment check requiring equal source and target decimal places.

impact.affected_asset: Target ERC-20 token inventory held by the migration lockbox and the economic value exchanged during migration.
impact.attacker_capability: A contract user can obtain the target payout computed from an unchanged integer amount after a source/target pair with unequal decimals has been configured; the report does not establish that an arbitrary user controls pair configuration.
impact.security_effect: Configured heterogeneous-decimal token pairs can cause an economically incorrect target-token payout, including target-token inflation/deflation and user loss.

causal_trace.summary: The deployment can configure source and target ERC-20 tokens with unequal decimal places.
The intended 1:1 economic migration assumes equal decimal domains, but the contract does not ensure the source and target tokens have identical decimal places.

migrate(uint256) passes the caller-supplied integer amount unchanged to _withdraw(i_targetToken, _msgSender(), amount), thereby transferring target-token base units using a source-token-denominated integer.

For an 18-decimal source and 6-decimal target, 1×10^18 source units results in 1×10^18 target units, stated as 1×10^12 target tokens; the reverse direction severely under-delivers. The report identifies financial loss and unintended inflation or deflation.

failure.operation: _withdraw(i_targetToken, _msgSender(), amount) with the unscaled source-token amount

primary_invariant.statement: A same-integer 1:1 migration is valid only when the configured source and target ERC-20 tokens use equal decimal precision.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The migration path treats the source amount integer as an equal amount of target-token base units without decimal conversion or a configuration-time equality check.

provenance.source_id: Sigma Prime Chainlink Migration Lockbox Security Assessment Report v2.1, MGL-01

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report provides the MGL-01 mechanism, quantitative decimal examples, recommended equality check, and reports resolution at commit fc7a2d7. The bundle has no direct source snapshot, fix diff, decimal-mismatch regression test, or issue-specific transaction execution trace. Appendix test output is present but does not establish execution of this finding; therefore no harness/oracle is claimed. Magnitude depends on the configured token pair and target liquidity.

remediation.invariant_restored: Deployment rejects a source/target pair unless sourceToken.decimals() equals targetToken.decimals(), so equal base-unit integers denote the same decimal scale.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: A source/target pair with different ERC-20 decimal precision must already be configured, and target-token inventory must be available for withdrawal.
data_structure_invariants: The source and target tokens must have matching decimal places when migration transfers the same base-unit integer.
The source amount integer must not be interpreted as an economically equivalent target amount across unequal decimal domains.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Caller supplies an amount in source-token base units; economic discrepancy occurs only where configured source and target decimal scales differ.
numeric_domains.name: amount

state_context.state_machine: A token pair is configured for a migration lockbox; users subsequently submit source-token amounts to migrate.
